findings.title: Partition lock creation is racy
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock does get then setdefault on partition_locks dict with no global lock. Two threads for the same new Partition can both miss the get and create different Lock objects, so add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets for that partition can run under different locks. Consequence is corrupted all_offsets/outstanding sets and wrong committable offsets, causing duplicate processing or skipping offsets.

findings.title: Commit scan loops over offset gaps
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets iterates range(start, max_offset+1) to find contiguous completion. If offsets are sparse (e.g. 100 and 1_000_100 after a gap, filtering, or different assignment), it loops ~1M times per partition on every 1s commit tick. Consequence is CPU burn and stalled commit thread, delaying all commits.

findings.title: Failed work is still marked complete and committed
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. The class docstring claims only successful processing is committed. Consequence is a poison or transient failure advances the committed offset past the failed message, so the message is lost with no retry or DLQ.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize while claiming natural backpressure. If a queue's worker stalls on a slow subscription, submit keeps appending via non-blocking put. Consequence is unbounded memory growth and OOM, instead of blocking the Arroyo poll loop.

findings.title: Shutdown abandons queued work
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run exits when that flag is set after the current item. Remaining queued WorkItems are never processed and their offsets never completed. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close calls this path, so normal close/rebalance drops in-memory work and forces redelivery or stalls commits.

findings.title: Shared queue pool is shut down by per-partition strategy
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py create_thread_queue_parallel_worker shares factory.queue_pool across all strategies from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate calls queue_pool.shutdown. Closing one partition assignment (e.g. on rebalance) kills workers for all current and future assignments reusing the factory pool, after which submit either blocks or raises queue.ShutDown and messages stop being processed.

findings.title: join ignores timeout and always closes
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) ignores the timeout argument and unconditionally calls close, which joins the commit thread for 5s and shuts down the pool. Callers expecting Arroyo join semantics (wait up to timeout without destroying the strategy) instead get a destructive shutdown.

findings.title: wait_until_empty ignores in-flight work
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty and get_stats use only Queue.qsize. An item taken by a worker but not yet finished or offset-completed leaves qsize at 0. Consequence is callers conclude processing is done while work is still in flight, causing premature commits checks and flaky tests.
